rationale: While studies confirm that pathogenic RNU2-2 variants cluster within conserved functional 5' domains (such as spliceosomal interaction regions) and recurrent de novo variants can cause a severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) with status epilepticus, profound impairment, and hyperkinesia, the hypothesis of uniform, highly congruent severe phenotypes driven strictly by de novo variants is contradicted by several major findings. First, comprehensive systematic cohort analyses demonstrate that biallelic (recessive) inheritance is at least twice as prevalent as the dominant de novo form, with distinct transcriptomic and stability mechanisms. Second, phenotypic expressivity is not uniformly severe DEE: phenotypes span a gradient-of-impact from DEE to mild learning disability without epilepsy (including dominant carriers without seizures).

evidence.text: Pathogenic variants in RNU2-2 cause a severe DEE characterized by median seizure onset at 24 months, focal and generalized seizures, status epilepticus, severe to profound impairment, sleep-activated multifocal epileptiform discharges on EEG, and hippocampal sclerosis on MRI.

source.title: Pathogenic Variants in RNU2‐2, a Non‐coding Spliceosomal RNA, Cause a Distinctive Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
source.quote: We identified recurrent pathogenic RNU2-2 variants in 4 of 672 (0.6%) patients with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) of unknown cause. An additional patient was subsequently included. Patients with RNU2-2 DEE had median seizure onset age of 24 months, focal and generalized seizures, status epilepticus (n = 5), severe to profound impairment, hyperventilation (n = 3), and obstructive sleep apnea (n = 3). Electroencephalography showed sleep-activated multifocal epileptiform discharges (n = 4) and hippocampal sclerosis on magnetic resonance imaging (n = 3).

source.title: Phenotypic and transcriptomic characterization of biallelic RNU2‐2 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
source.quote: We identified 14 individuals from nine families with 12 ultra-rare biallelic RNU2-2 variants clustering in the conserved 5' domains... All individuals presented with a highly concordant, severe DEE, characterized by severe to profound intellectual disability, inability to walk or communicate, hyperkinesia, and refractory seizures. Infantile spasms and tonic seizures were the predominant seizure types and a Lennox-Gastaut syndrome-like phenotype was common.

source.title: Systematic analysis of snRNA genes reveals frequent RNU2-2 variants in dominant and recessive developmental and epileptic encephalopathies
source.quote: We report RNU2-2 variants in 141 individuals, including 35 with recurrent dominant pathogenic variants and 91 affected members from 73 families with biallelic variants. Recessive RNU2-2 NDD is at least twice as frequent as the dominant form... Among the 16 patients without epilepsy, 4 had dominant pathogenic variants... Our results support a gradient-of-impact model bridging dominant and recessive inheritance...

evidence.text: Recessive RNU2-2 syndrome caused by biallelic variants represents an extraordinarily frequent NDD category that is clinically, genetically, and mechanistically distinct from dominant RNU2-2 disorder, operating through compromised transcript stability rather than simple single dominant-negative catalytic disruption.

source.title: Biallelic variants in RNU2-2 cause a remarkably frequent developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
source.quote: We show that the recessive RNU2-2 syndrome is genetically, clinically and mechanistically distinct from the dominant RNU2-2 disorder. Within our cohort, the recessive RNU2-2 syndrome emerges as by far the most frequent recessive NDD, greatly disproportionate to the small genomic footprint of this non-protein-coding gene.

conflicts: Dominant de novo variants do not exclusively cause a uniform, severe DEE; phenotypes span a continuum down to mild learning disability without epilepsy (4/16 non-epileptic patients carried dominant pathogenic variants in Leitão et al.).

The disease architecture is not dominated exclusively by recurrent de novo mutations; recessive biallelic RNU2-2 alterations occur at more than double the frequency of dominant variants in large cohorts (91 biallelic vs 35 dominant cases in Leitão et al.) and represent a distinct molecular mechanism involving reduced U2-2 stability.

new_directions.question_text: What specific nucleotide-level or structural features distinguish RNU2-2 variants that manifest as dominant DEE from those that cause mild intellectual disability without epilepsy or require biallelic transmission?
new_directions.rationale: Large cohort studies demonstrate a gradient of clinical severity across dominant and recessive forms, suggesting subtle positional or functional determinants govern phenotypic penetration.

new_directions.question_text: Can tissue-specific mis-splicing profiles in accessible patient cells reliably differentiate RNU2-2 encephalopathy from phenocopying spliceosomopathies such as ReNU syndrome (RNU4-2)?
new_directions.rationale: Fibroblast RNA sequencing reveals distinct alternative 3' splice site usage and mutually exclusive exon events in RNU2-2, but these signatures are suppressed or absent in blood cells.
